WP13's five rulings, at cc's ask (2026-11-03 08:01Z), under hv's simpler-or-easier rule. (1) Sequencing, as cc proposes. The parity record carries verdicts only (the command, same or different, the exit codes), never output text: a difference is named by its kind, and the scratch outputs are deleted once the verdicts are written (D11). Rows that need Contacts or Full Disk Access are recorded as not run; cc's parity runner takes a row list, so hv can run those rows in hv's own terminal, and AC-00.5 waits for them. CI runs bin/devbin check nopython beside the other devbin steps, because CI runs the checks one by one, not check all. The guard's tests compare no hand-written count. It runs on both runners. Three conditions keep each part from passing vacuously. Part 1: SidecarStore::new on a missing sidecar refuses, naming bin/devbin build, and the path is still absent after. Part 2: a stand-in sidecar driven through every read the store makes records each of dump, backup and group, and nothing else; two measured mutants (the allowed set without group, and the group read dropped) show both halves can fail. Part 3: it reads the mode switch in swift/pplr-contacts/main.swift, fails naming why when it finds none, and compares the labels as a set with the three names, never as a count. The row's note names AT-10.1 and AT-11.1 for 'only through the store interface', and src/contacts/json.rs's unit tests for the dump format.
